segments.description: Marina beach in Chennai along the Bay of Bengal is India's longest and world's second longest beach. segments.name: Vadapalani Murugan Temple
segments.description: The Arulmigu Vadapalani Murugan Temple is a famous Hindu temple in Chennai, dedicated to Lord Murugan. It was founded in the late 19th century from a humble thatched hut and is now a grand temple known for its divine power, architectural details like the Rajagopuram with Skanda Purana scenes, and a unique idol of Lord Murugan wearing footwear, symbolizing his eagerness to help devotees. The temple complex includes numerous shrines to other deities, a temple tank, and large halls for events.

segments.name: T Nagar (only for Shopping)
segments.description: T. Nagar (Thyagaraya Nagar) is a bustling, well-planned commercial and residential hub in Chennai, known for being one of the city's primary shopping districts, especially for textiles and jewelry. Developed in the 1920s, it is a densely populated area with a high concentration of retail stores and businesses, including the famous Ranganathan Street and Pondy Bazaar. Despite its commercial nature, it also serves as a residential area and is well-connected by road, rail, and metro.

segments.name: Mahabalipuram  Group of Monuments
segments.description: Mahabalipuram (or Mamallapuram), located along southeastern India's Coromandel Coast, was a celebrated port city of the Pallavas. The group of monuments there consists of rock-cut cave temples, monolithic temples, bas-relief sculptures, and structural temples as well as the excavated remains of temples. The Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram includes several categories of 7th and 8th-century CE structures built by the Pallava dynasty, such as the monolithic Pancha Rathas (Five Chariots), the Shore Temple, rock-cut caves (mandapas), and large rock reliefs like the Descent of the Ganges. Other notable monuments are the Tiger Cave, Arjuna's Penance (another name for the Descent of the Ganges), and several excavated temples.
